2027-02-09.title: Tuesday of the first week of the Great Fast
readings: The covenant sacrifice: Abram keeps watch
No condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus
2027-02-09.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
theo: Abram has believed, but he still asks: “O Lord God, how am I to know that I shall possess it?” God does not scold him. He asks for a sacrifice: a heifer, a goat, a ram, a turtledove and a pigeon. Abram cuts the animals in two and waits, and “when birds of prey came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away.” Then darkness falls, and God speaks of the long road ahead: his descendants will be strangers and slaves for four hundred years, and then come out free. Faith is not the end of questions; it is staying beside the sacrifice and driving away whatever would snatch it. In the Fast our prayer, fasting and almsgiving are such an offering, and the birds of prey are many: distraction, discouragement, the voice that says it is useless.

Paul tells us why we can keep watch without fear: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.” The Fast is not an attempt to earn God's love by our own strength; it is letting the Spirit who dwells in us set our minds “on the things of the Spirit”, which are “life and peace.” And in the Gospel Jesus shows whose sacrifice saves us: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” Unlike the hired hand, he does not run when the wolf comes. He knows his own, and he will bring the other sheep too, “so there will be one flock, one shepherd.” St Gregory the Great says that the Good Shepherd first did what he taught: he laid down his life (in substance).

“The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
live: Name the one distraction that most steals your prayer, and drive it away today.

2027-02-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you laid down your life for us and took away our condemnation. Pour your Spirit into our hearts, so that we may keep watch over the offering of this Fast and drive away all that would steal it. Gather all your sheep into one flock, and keep us close to your voice. Amen.
altar: The Good Shepherd who laid down his life feeds his flock at the altar with his own Body and Blood.

quick: Abram offered a sacrifice and drove away the birds of prey.

Jesus is the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep.
2027-02-09.action: Drive away one distraction from your prayer today.
2027-02-09.question: What birds of prey come down on my fast?

family.explain: A good shepherd knows each of his sheep by name and protects them from the wolf. Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He knows each of us and gave his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, who are shepherds in Jesus' name.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen better to Jesus' voice during the Fast?”

illus: A goatherd in the hills near Idukki was asked by a visiting boy how he could tell his forty goats apart. He laughed and called one name. A small brown goat lifted its head and came running. He said: I have named every one. When the rain is heavy I carry the weak ones on my shoulders. They know my voice because they know I will not leave them.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, we are your sheep. Let us hear your voice. Amen.
share: How am I to know? (Genesis 15:8). What question do I bring to God in this Fast?
To set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace (Romans 8:6). What fills my mind most of the day?
I know my own and my own know me (John 10:14). Do I know the Shepherd's voice?
interc: For our bishops and priests, shepherds of the flock.
For those who have wandered from the Church.
For Christians separated from one another, that there may be one flock.
For those who feel condemned and without hope.
For all who are keeping the Fast with difficulty.
pm.close: Father, your Son laid down his life for his sheep. Keep us in his flock, free from condemnation and alive in the Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abram believed God and yet asked: how am I to know? God answered with a covenant. Abram prepared the sacrifice, and when birds of prey came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away (Genesis 15:8, 11).
Our Fast is an offering, and birds of prey come to snatch it: distraction, discouragement, the voice that says it is useless. Like Abram, we must keep watch.
But we do not keep watch in fear. There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:1). The Spirit of life dwells in us.
And Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). His sacrifice saves us; ours is only to stay close to him and listen to his voice. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the Good Shepherd. He knows your name, he takes care of you, and he even gave his life for you. In the Fast, let us listen to his voice by reading the Bible.
